map.X̄ 控制图界限计算器求子组均值控制图的 3σ 上下控制限，适合统计过程控制（S: The X-bar chart limits calculator finds the 3σ control limits of a subgroup-mean chart, suited to monitoring mean stability and detecting outliers in SPC.
map.σ=2、n=5 → 界限 ±2.683。 σ/√n 为均值标准误。: σ=2, n=5 → limits ±2.683. σ/√n is the standard error of the mean.
map.子组均值控制图的 3σ 控制界限。: The 3σ control limits of a subgroup-mean chart.
map.为均值控制图（X̄图）计算中心线 CL 与控制限 UCL/LCL，监控过程均值是: Compute center line CL and control limits UCL/LCL for the mean chart (X-bar), monitoring whether the process mean is in control and has special-cause variation.
map.过程能力研究前先确认过程稳定（受控），否则能力指数无意义。: Before capability study, confirm the process is stable (in control); otherwise capability indices are meaningless.
map.子组容量变化时（n 不同），按 √n 更新标准误与界限。: When subgroup size changes (different n), update standard error and limits by √n.
map.：标准误 SE = σ/√n（σ 为过程标准差，n 为子组容量）；中心线 CL: : Standard error SE = σ/√n (σ is the process std dev, n the subgroup size); center line CL = μ (process target/mean); control limits UCL = μ + 3·SE, LCL = μ − 3·SE (3σ rule, ~0.27% false-alarm rate). When σ is unknown, estimate via subgroup range mean R̄/d₂.
map.：过程目标 μ=50、σ=2、子组容量 n=5：SE = 2/√5 ≈ 0.89: : Process target μ=50, σ=2, subgroup size n=5: SE = 2/√5 ≈ 0.8944; UCL = 50 + 3×0.8944 ≈ 52.683, LCL = 50 − 3×0.8944 ≈ 47.317, CL = 50.000. If a subgroup mean falls outside [47.317, 52.683], it triggers an out-of-control signal—investigate special causes rather than immediately adjusting the machine.
map.公式里的 σ 用哪个？: Which σ goes in the formula?
map.控制图限用『过程固有标准差』估计（如 R̄/d₂ 或 S̄/c₄），反映受控下的: Control limits use the 'inherent process std dev' estimate (e.g., R̄/d₂ or S̄/c₄), reflecting common-cause variation under control; don't use the overall sample std dev (special causes inflate σ, widen limits, and miss anomalies).
map.子组容量 n 越大控制限越窄吗？: Do larger subgroup size n make limits narrower?
map.是的。SE = σ/√n，n 越大 SE 越小、控制限越窄，对均值漂移越敏感；但: Yes. SE = σ/√n, larger n gives smaller SE and narrower limits, more sensitive to mean shift; but too large n increases detection lag and cost—commonly 4–5, larger for critical processes.
